name: Beverage Finder by Taps + Tables
author: BevFinder

sections.description:
Beverage Finder is a beer finder, beverage finder, and store locator for breweries, wineries, distilleries, and beverage brands. Show customers where to buy your products with an interactive map and searchable list of retail locations.

Features

  • Interactive Google Map with a sortable list of nearby locations
  • CSV import (works with Encompass sales reports or the included template)
  • Edit any location in the admin: name, address, products, and coordinates
  • Delete and restore locations one at a time, in bulk, or all at once
  • Setup checklist that shows exactly what’s left to do
  • Optional one-click address-to-coordinates lookup with a beveragefinder.net account
  • Download all of your locations as a CSV
  • Brand/product filter
  • Visitor location via the browser’s built-in geolocation (no API needed)
  • Custom map pin
  • Location expiration based on last delivery date
  • Unlimited locations
  • Responsive and mobile friendly
  • Works great as a beer finder or product locator
  • Find your product at stores, bars, restaurants, or other retailer

How it works

Import a CSV that includes latitude and longitude for each location. Locations appear on the map immediately. Re-importing updates delivery dates and coordinates for existing retailer/brand combinations instead of creating duplicates.

Only have street addresses? You can look up coordinates yourself on Google Maps, fill them in with any geocoding tool and re-import, or connect an optional beveragefinder.net account and click Get Coordinates on the BevFinder → Get Lat / Long screen. The account is a paid service with a free starter plan. Everything else in the plugin works fully without it, and the plugin only contacts beveragefinder.net when you click one of its buttons.

External Services

This plugin connects to the Google Maps Platform to display the map, and — only if you choose to — to beveragefinder.net to convert addresses into coordinates.

Google Maps JavaScript API (Google LLC)

  • What it’s used for: rendering the interactive map, location markers, and the “your location” marker icon.
  • When data is sent: every time a visitor views a page containing the [beverage_finder] shortcode.
  • What is sent: your Maps API key, the page’s referring URL, the visitor’s IP address and browser details (as part of any request to Google), and the map coordinates being displayed.
  • Terms of Service: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

The visitor’s own location (if they allow it) is read by their browser and sent only to your WordPress site to sort results by distance.

beveragefinder.net address lookup (Taps + Tables)

  • What it’s used for: converting the street addresses of your locations into latitude/longitude, and showing your plan’s usage. beveragefinder.net uses the US Census Geocoder, with the Google Geocoding API as a fallback.
  • When data is sent: only when a site administrator saves a beveragefinder.net WordPress API Key on BevFinder → Get Lat / Long and then clicks Get Coordinates or Check account. Nothing is sent automatically, on a schedule, or from the front end.
  • What is sent: the WordPress API Key, your site URL, the plugin version, and the street address, city, state, and ZIP of locations that have no coordinates (or whose Google-provided coordinates are more than 30 days old, which Google’s terms require be refreshed). Retailer names, products, and sales data are not sent.
  • Terms of Service: https://beveragefinder.net/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://beveragefinder.net/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to BevFinder → Instructions and follow the setup checklist.
  4. Enter your Google Maps JavaScript API key on BevFinder → Settings.
  5. Import your locations CSV on BevFinder → Locations.
  6. Add the [beverage_finder] shortcode to any page or post.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Google Maps API key?

Yes. The map is displayed with the Google Maps JavaScript API. Create a key in the Google Cloud Console, enable the Maps JavaScript API, restrict the key to your domain, and paste it into BevFinder → Settings.

What CSV format is required?

Use the template included in the plugin (BevFinder → Instructions → Download the CSV template). Columns, in order:

Distributor Number, Distributor Retailer ID, Retailer Name, Address, City, State, Zip, Distributor Product Num, Supplier Product Num, Brand Name, Product Name, On/Off Premise, Salesperson, Delivery Date, Latitude, Longitude

Rows without latitude/longitude are imported but won’t show on the map until coordinates are added.

How do I find latitude and longitude?

Search the address on Google Maps, right-click the pin, and click the coordinates to copy them (for example 37.7749, -122.4194), then paste them into the location on BevFinder → Locations → Edit.

For many addresses, connect a beveragefinder.net account on BevFinder → Get Lat / Long and click Get Coordinates. Each unique address is one lookup, and the free plan includes 10 a month. Addresses that already have coordinates are never sent, except Google-placed coordinates older than 30 days, which Google’s terms require be refreshed.

Is there a location limit?

No. Import as many locations as you like.

How does location expiration work?

Locations whose last delivery date is older than the number of days set in Expire Locations After are hidden from the map. Importing a newer delivery date shows them again. Set the value to 0 to never expire locations.

Can I fix a location without re-importing?

Yes. On BevFinder → Locations, search for it and click Edit. You can change the retailer name, address, brand and product names, coordinates, and whether it shows on the map.

The retailer name, address, and coordinates apply to every product at that location, so you only fix a moved store once. Edited locations are marked “Edited” in the list, and later CSV imports won’t overwrite them — imports only refresh their delivery date.

What happens when I delete locations?

They are removed from your map but not erased. Deleted locations are listed under Locations → Deleted, where you can restore them individually, in bulk, or all at once with Restore All. Re-importing a CSV also restores any matching deleted rows. Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen permanently removes all location data.

Is BevFinder Pro required?

No. BevFinder Pro is the optional beveragefinder.net account that converts addresses to coordinates for you. Importing, editing, and mapping unlimited locations is free.

Can I customize the map pin?

Yes. Upload an image in BevFinder → Settings (minimum 44 x 60 px).
sections.changelog:
2.3.0

  • New admin layout with tabs: Instructions, Settings, Locations, Get Lat / Long, and BevFinder Pro.
  • Instructions now include a live setup checklist and a full CSV column reference.
  • Locations: Active, Not on map, and Deleted views with counts; select rows to delete or restore them.
  • Added Restore All. Delete All now clearly explains that deleted locations can be restored.
  • Import summary links straight to getting coordinates for rows that don’t have any.
  • Optional: connect a beveragefinder.net account and click Get Coordinates to fill in missing latitude/longitude.
  • Addresses that can’t be found are flagged so they aren’t looked up again until you fix them.
  • Coordinates placed by Google are refreshed after 30 days when you next click Get Coordinates, as Google’s terms require.
  • Download My Locations now exports active locations only.
  • Settings and Get Coordinates links on the Plugins screen.

2.2.0

  • Added a searchable location list with editing for name, address, products, coordinates, and map visibility.
  • Edits to a retailer name, address, or coordinates now apply to every product at that location.
  • Hand-edited locations are marked “Edited” and are no longer overwritten by CSV imports (delivery dates still refresh).
  • Added “Download My Locations (CSV)” in the same column order as the import template.
  • Added a Show/Hide button for the Google Maps API key.
  • Map now pans with one finger; the scroll wheel scrolls the page and the +/- buttons zoom.

2.1.0

  • CSV import now reads Latitude and Longitude columns.
  • Location expiration now filters by last delivery date.
  • Re-importing a deleted location restores it.
  • Import requires a valid nonce and the manage_options capability.
  • All database queries use prepared statements with identifier placeholders.
  • Map info windows escape all location data.
  • Removed unused settings and legacy code.

2.0.0

  • Simplified admin panel.
  • Fixed map display issue.
